data.title: Choose the correct answer for each question.
data.description: Practise discourse markers that organise argument, signal viewpoint, reformulate ideas and guide the reader through complex texts.
learningPoints: Use markers to signal contrast, addition, reformulation and exemplification.
Use expressions such as in other words, for instance and in particular accurately.
Use on balance and overall to evaluate or conclude.
Use admittedly to acknowledge a point before qualifying it.
Match discourse markers to the logical function they perform.
Use punctuation and sentence position appropriately.

sections.explain: IN OTHER WORDS restates an idea more clearly or simply.

words.word: The policy is not sustainable. In other words, it cannot continue in its current form.
The policy is not sustainable. For example, it cannot continue in its current form as a restatement.
The policy is not sustainable in other words because it cannot continue.
Several changes could help. For instance, the company could offer flexible hours.
Several changes could help. On balance, the company could offer flexible hours as an example.
Several changes could help for instance because flexible hours.

sections.explain: IN PARTICULAR highlights one especially relevant item.

words.word: Many sectors were affected, in particular tourism and hospitality.
Many sectors were affected, in contrast tourism and hospitality.
Many sectors were affected, in particular but tourism and hospitality.

sections.explain: ADMITTEDLY acknowledges a point before a qualification or contrast.

words.word: Admittedly, the plan is expensive, but it could save money in the long term.
Admittedly, the plan is expensive, therefore it could save money in the long term as a concession.
Admittedly but the plan is expensive, however because it could save money.

sections.explain: ON BALANCE introduces a considered overall judgment.

words.word: On balance, the advantages outweigh the disadvantages.
For example, the advantages outweigh the disadvantages as an overall judgment.
On balance because the advantages outweigh the disadvantages.

sections.explain: OVERALL introduces a general summary or evaluation.

words.word: Overall, the project was successful despite several delays.
In particular, the project was successful despite several delays as a general summary.
Overall however because the project was successful.

sections.explain: BY CONTRAST highlights a clear difference from the previous idea.

words.word: City rents have risen sharply. By contrast, prices in rural areas have remained stable.
City rents have risen sharply. As a result, prices in rural areas have remained stable as a contrast.
City rents have risen sharply by contrast because rural prices remained stable.

sections.explain: TO SOME EXTENT limits or qualifies a claim.

words.word: To some extent, the criticism is justified.
In other words, the criticism is justified, meaning only partly.
To some extent because the criticism is justified.

sections.summary: Using 'in fact' for correction or emphasis.
sections.explain: IN FACT can strengthen, correct or clarify a previous statement.

words.word: The journey wasn't difficult. In fact, it was surprisingly easy.
The journey wasn't difficult. Nevertheless, it was surprisingly easy as emphasis rather than contrast.
The journey wasn't difficult in fact but because it was easy.

sections.summary: Using discourse markers to guide argument.
sections.explain: A discourse marker should match the rhetorical function of the sentence.

words.word: There are some drawbacks. Nevertheless, the proposal is worth considering.
There are some drawbacks. For instance, the proposal is worth considering as a concession.
There are some drawbacks nevertheless because the proposal is worth considering.
